# Dealroom — LLM Context

> Dealroom is a two-party asynchronous contract negotiation platform built by TODO.LAW. It replaces emailing Word files back and forth with a shared workspace that proposes a compromise for each clause using a fixed, published weighted formula (no AI model decides the outcome).

## Hosted and the kit

- **dealroom.todo.law charges per contract.** Drafting and negotiating are free. Each contract is paid once, at the price shown on the pricing page, when it is first downloaded (PDF, DOCX or TXT) or when its signature starts. Every contract skill, premium ones included, is covered by that price. There is no monthly plan.
- **Agents pay per contract too.** An agent pays for each contract with one prepaid credit: a contract made in one call spends it when it is made, and a negotiated contract spends it when its document is first fetched. Credits are sold in packs of ten and belong to the customer account, so any of its API keys can spend them. The current amounts are in the agent card (/.well-known/agent.json, under "pricing").
- **An agent's API key is created by its user, without contacting us.** Sign in at https://dealroom.todo.law, open Settings, API keys (https://dealroom.todo.law/settings/api-keys) and choose Create key. The full key (it starts with drk_) is shown once, so copy it then. The same page lists your keys with their last use, revokes them, shows the credit balance and sells credit packs. An account can hold up to 5 active keys.
- **The kit (self-hosted Dealroom) has no caps.** Premium skills are sold only for the kit: 60 a year each in the kit (in your currency), bought on the todo.law storefront and activated offline with a licence file.

## Make a contract in one call (developers and agents)

- **Quick start:** https://dealroom.todo.law/developers (Spanish: https://dealroom.todo.law/es/developers). Three steps: create an API key at /settings/api-keys, buy credits on the same page, make the call. Plain Markdown of the same page: https://dealroom.todo.law/developers.md (Spanish: https://dealroom.todo.law/es/developers.md), with every contract type in a table.
- **One REST call:** `POST https://dealroom.todo.law/api/v1/agent/contracts` with `Authorization: Bearer drk_...` and a JSON body: `contractType` (code such as `NDA`, or the guide slug such as `nda`), `party` (your side: `legalName`, optional `address`, `taxId`, `signatoryName`, `signatoryTitle`, `email`), optional `counterparty` (same shape; left out, the other side's block stays blank), `governingLaw` (needed only when the type offers more than one), optional `language`, `role` (DPA and BAA), `terms` (inputs by id), `clauses` (clause id to option code) and `inline` (`md`, `html` or `txt`: the contract itself in the answer). Clauses left out take the standard option. The answer gives `dealId`, `dealUrl` (to read it in Dealroom), the Markdown, HTML, TXT, PDF and DOCX links and, with `inline`, the contract.
- **Formats:** every contract can be fetched as Markdown (`/api/v1/agent/deals/{dealId}/document/md`, best for agents), self-contained HTML (`/document/html`, one section per clause with stable ids), plain text (`/document/txt`), PDF (`/document`) or DOCX (`/document/docx`). All come from the same contract text; once the contract is paid, every format is free.
- **What it costs:** the same as any contract. One prepaid credit is spent; with no credit the answer is HTTP 402 with code PAYMENT_REQUIRED and nothing is created. Later downloads of the same contract are free. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on retries so a retry is not charged again.
- **What each type needs:** `GET https://dealroom.todo.law/api/v1/agent/contract-types` (no key; `?lang=es` for Spanish): codes, slugs, governing laws, languages, roles and inputs. Send every required input in `terms`; a required input with a default can be left out and the default is applied.
- **MCP server:** `https://dealroom.todo.law/api/v1/agent/mcp` (Streamable HTTP; API key in the Authorization header). Its 13 tools: `list_contract_types` (no key needed), `generate_contract` (returns the contract as Markdown by default), `download_contract` (Markdown by default; also HTML, PDF, DOCX, TXT), `get_deal`, `delete_deal` (deletes one of your single-party deals and its data; REST `DELETE /api/v1/agent/deals/:id`), `buy_credits`, `get_credit_balance`, `get_subscriptions` (earlier per-skill subscriptions; every template is now included), and for negotiation between two agents `list_templates`, `get_template`, `create_playbook`, `initiate_negotiation` and `join_negotiation` (these also take the A2A_ agent-to-agent protocol types, which are negotiated only). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http dealroom https://dealroom.todo.law/api/v1/agent/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer drk_YOUR_KEY"`. Setup for Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code is on the quick start page.
- **Discovery files:** MCP server card https://dealroom.todo.law/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, MCP discovery https://dealroom.todo.law/.well-known/mcp.json, agent card https://dealroom.todo.law/.well-known/agent.json (it describes the service; Dealroom is reached through the MCP server or the REST API, not the A2A protocol), and the full list of contract types with codes, required inputs, guide links and a one-call body for each at https://dealroom.todo.law/llms-full.txt.
- **Per contract:** every contract guide below opens with a "Make this contract from your AI agent" block: the code to send as `contractType`, the required inputs, the MCP server address and the one call filled in for that contract (anchor `#agent`, for example https://dealroom.todo.law/contracts/nda#agent).

## Contract Guides

One page per contract type, in English and Castilian Spanish: what the contract is, who signs it, the key clauses, what the two sides usually negotiate and the middle ground Dealroom proposes, supported jurisdictions, common mistakes, and how to create it in Dealroom or through the agent API (`GET /api/v1/agent/templates?q=nda`, MCP `list_templates` with `query`; one-call creation with `POST /api/v1/agent/contracts` or MCP `generate_contract`).

## What Dealroom Does

- **Two-Party Negotiation**: Asynchronous contract negotiation between two parties on a shared workspace
- **Weighted Compromise**: A fixed formula, stake = ((5 - flexibility) / 5 × 0.6) + (|bias| × 0.4), proposes a compromise for each clause from each party's firmness and the bias of each option; it is documented at /docs/compromise
- **Access and transport**: Connections use HTTPS; access to each deal is checked on the server and only the deal's parties can download its documents. Contract content is stored in the service's database and is not end-to-end encrypted
- **Cross-Border Ready**: Supports California, England & Wales, and Spain jurisdictions
- **Contract Types**: 37 contract types, each with a guide listed above, including NDA, MSA, SaaS Agreement, DPA, Privacy Notice, Joint Venture, Employment, Consulting, and more
- **Export & Sign**: Generate final documents for signing after negotiation completes
- **A2A Agent Protocol**: Machine-readable agent card at /.well-known/agent.json for agent-to-agent negotiation
- **MCP server**: https://dealroom.todo.law/api/v1/agent/mcp, listed in the MCP registry as io.github.sergiomaldo/dealroom

## TODO.LAW Ecosystem

Dealroom is part of the TODO.LAW platform for AI-native legal services:

- **Dealroom** (dealroom.todo.law) — Contract negotiation
- **DPO Central** (dpocentral.todo.law) — Privacy compliance management
- **AI Sentinel** (aisentinel.todo.law) — AI governance and EU AI Act compliance
- **Seneca** (seneca.todo.law) — Privacy litigation research
- **Vendor.Watch** (vendor.watch) — SaaS vendor compliance database
- **Clausemaster** (clausemaster.todo.law) — AI-powered contract analysis
- **Gavel** (gavel.todo.law) — Digital arbitration protocol

For full ecosystem context, see: https://todo.law/llms-full.txt
